first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and prior evidence supports simplifying signup and onboarding to improve time-to-value. A small guarded test is preferable to a broad rollout, with qualified-revenue and lead-quality checks to detect whether lower friction attracts lower-value accounts. This directly addresses two current funnel problems while preserving uncertainty about the competitor-driven pricing pressure.

mid.rationale: Run a small guarded onboarding-shortening experiment because it directly addresses the 4% completion decline and 6% activation decline, with strong prior evidence of higher completion, faster time-to-value, and better 30-day retention. Include qualified revenue, segment mix, activation, and retention guardrails; the SMB signup evidence includes a 1% retention decline and did not generalize beyond SMB, so avoid a broad signup change or rollout.

final2.rationale: The competitor's deeper cut and doubled churn conversations create an immediate, segment-specific revenue threat. Test targeted promotional pricing only for demonstrably price-sensitive SMB accounts rather than broad discounting, using margin, qualified revenue, retention, and conversion guardrails. Prior memory supports acquisition and revenue lift in this segment, but the archived source was not verified this cycle, so keep the response controlled and preserve uncertainty while continuing to monitor the onboarding experiment separately.
